newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech FinMin Kocarnik says weaker crown positive.
newsitem.headline: Czech FinMin Kocarnik says weaker crown positive.

text.p: A weaker Czech crown is better for the economy, but the course of its value lies in the hands of the central bank and not the government, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said on Tuesday.
"It is certainly better (weaker) than if the crown was much stronger. It is certainly better right now for the economy," he told a banking conference in the Czech city of Brno.
"The crown a little bit on the depreciation side of the band is definitely positive," he added.
Kocarnik refused to comment further on exchange rate policy, adding that it was up to the central bank to determine monetary policy.
The central bank fixes the crown daily within a +/-7.5 percent fluctuation band of its dollar/mark basket midpoint.
Last week the government announced a sweeping series of measures aimed at reviving the economy and stopping a widening trade deficit.
The trade gap hit a record 160.3 billion crowns in 1996, pushing the current account and balance of payments into deficits as well.
Earlier on Tuesday the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) released better-than-expected first quarter trade figures, which Kocarnik called "pleasing".
The trade deficit for the first three months of the year was 40.2 billion crowns, up from 27.1 billion in the first quarter of 1996.
The trade gap for March only of some 13.4 billion crowns, however, was better-than-expected, with some analysts forecasting on Monday a shortfall of as much as 18 billion crowns.
